issues.claim: "177 Google reviews average 5.0" (audit opener, and the same figure underpins the profile's review positioning)
issues.problem: Re-opening the cited Trustindex page shows 182 reviews at 5.0/5 (99% five-star), described as collected from Google and Trustindex. The 5.0 average is confirmed; the count 177 is stale and the source is not purely Google. A live counter the owner can check on their own screen should not be quoted as a precise figure.
issues.fix: Replace with a rounded, source-safe phrasing such as "a 5.0 average across more than 180 reviews (Google/Trustindex)" or drop the count entirely and keep "5.0 average". If a precise figure is kept, date it ("182 as of Nov 2026") and attribute it to Trustindex.

issues.claim: Opportunity 2: "8–15 questions a business day x 250 days = 2,000–3,750 ... x 30–50% self-service-answerable"
issues.problem: The 8–15 questions/day volume is an inference with no public source (the profile lists after-hours contact volume as unknown), but unlike the other two opportunities it is not tagged "our assumption". A reader can mistake it for a measured figure.
issues.fix: Add "our assumption" (or "our estimate") after "8–15 questions a business day", matching the labelling used in sections 1 and 3.

issues.claim: "one Jamesburg department handles them" (section 1) and "certificates run through CSR24" (walk-in opener)
issues.problem: The Jamesburg page confirms the entire Account Management department sits there, and the quote page confirms certificate requests are directed to the CSR24 portal. It does not state that that department personally drafts certificates, nor that all certificates "run through" CSR24. As written these read as stated fact rather than inference.
issues.fix: Soften to inference: "certificate requests are routed to CSR24, and the account management team that handles them sits in Jamesburg — worth confirming who drafts them." In the walk-in line, say "certificate requests go to your CSR24 portal" instead of "certificates run through CSR24".

issues.problem: Not a factual error: the audit's arithmetic is correct and its ranges are more conservative than analysis.json. But the two documents state different numbers for the same three opportunities, which will be visible if both are shown to the client.
issues.fix: No change needed in the audit; make sure any deck or follow-up material quotes the audit's conservative figures, or add one line noting the audit uses the tighter case.
